chapter.title: Adverbs and expressions of time, frequency, and location

sections.title: Adverbs and expressions of time and frequency
Interrogative forms; question words and adverbs of location

grammar_rules.title: Placement of adverbs of frequency and time
grammar_rules.summary: Short adverbs of frequency (souvent, toujours, jamais, bien, mal) immediately follow the conjugated verb; in compound tenses they sit between auxiliary and past participle.
grammar_rules.explanation:
- Simple tense: 'Il parle souvent français' (after verb).
- Compound tense: 'Il a souvent parlé français' (between auxiliary and participle).
- Time expressions (hier, demain, ce matin) usually sit at beginning or end of sentence.

common_mistakes.explanation: Adverbs follow conjugated verb in French.

grammar_rules.title: Interrogative question words (Où, Quand, Comment, Pourquoi, Combien)
grammar_rules.summary: Où (where), Quand (when), Comment (how), Pourquoi (why), Combien (how much/many), Qui (who), Que/Qu' (what).
grammar_rules.explanation:
Combined with est-ce que or inversion:
- 'Où habitez-vous?' / 'Où est-ce que vous habitez?'
- 'Pourquoi pars-tu?' / 'Pourquoi est-ce que tu pars?'

examples.french: Nous avons toujours aimé nous promener le long de la Seine.
examples.english: We have always loved taking walks along the Seine.
